title: Density of MgO
given: One mole of MgO fills a cube with side 22.37 mm. Find density in g/cm³.

steps.title: Find mass
steps.text: Add the molar masses of Mg and O.

steps.title: Find volume
steps.text: Convert the side to centimetres before cubing it.

title: Dimensions of a magnesium cube
given: Find the three dimensions of a cube containing 1 mol of solid Mg.

steps.title: Find the volume
steps.text: Use M = 24.305 g/mol and room-temperature density ρ = 1.74 g/cm³.

note: The handout does not supply magnesium’s density. This uses 1.74 g/cm³; use the course table if a different value is specified.

title: Angle between crystal directions
given: Find the angle between [110] and [111] in a cubic crystal.

steps.title: Write the vectors
steps.text: For cubic axes, use the indices as Cartesian components.

title: Plane intercepts
given: Find the axial intercepts of the (3, −1, 1) plane. The middle index has an overbar in the handout.

steps.title: Take reciprocals
steps.text: For Miller indices (hkl), the intercepts are a/h, b/k, and c/l.

title: Vacancy fraction at 660°C
given: At 400°C, f₁ = 2.29 × 10⁻⁵. Find f₂ at 660°C using Q = 0.76 eV and k = 8.62 × 10⁻⁵ eV/K.

steps.title: Divide the two vacancy equations
steps.text: Use f = A exp(−Q/kT). Taking a ratio removes the same prefactor A.

note: Using A = 1 would not reproduce the supplied starting fraction. The ratio method uses both the initial fraction and the lecture model.

title: Carbon diffusion time
given: Cₛ = 1.0 wt%, C₀ = 0.2 wt%, C = 0.6 wt%, x = 1 mm, and D = 2.98 × 10⁻¹¹ m²/s at 1000°C. Find time.

steps.title: Form the concentration ratio
steps.text: Use the constant-surface-concentration solution for a semi-infinite solid.

note: Assumes constant surface concentration, temperature and D, and one-dimensional diffusion into a thick solid.
